# Modeling and Results {#sec-model}

::: {.lead-text}
We trained three models to recognize which flood-related events became high-consequence. The inputs are what surrounds each event (terrain, streams, paved surfaces, community vulnerability, local flood history, and season), not the storm's own damage or death toll. The data were prepared in **R** and the models were fit in **Python (scikit-learn)**; both run in this one document through the `reticulate` package.
:::

## From R to Python

```{r}
#| label: py-setup
# Point reticulate at the project's conda environment before any Python runs.
# R's spatial packages and scikit-learn each bring their own OpenMP runtime;
# two runtimes in one process crash gradient boosting. Single-threaded OpenMP
# (set before Python starts) avoids the conflict.
Sys.setenv(OMP_NUM_THREADS = "1", KMP_DUPLICATE_LIB_OK = "TRUE")
library(reticulate)   # attaches `py`, R's view of Python objects
use_condaenv(p$python_env, required = TRUE)
paths$nri      <- rp(p$nri_path)
paths$explorer <- rp(p$explorer_path)
py_cfg <- reticulate::py_config()
tibble::tibble(
  item  = c("Python", "Environment", "Packages"),
  value = c(py_cfg$version_string |> sub(" \\|.*", "", x = _), p$python_env,
            "pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, shap, matplotlib")
) |> knitr::kable(col.names = NULL)
```

The event table built in the earlier sections lives in R. Two model inputs are added in R before the hand-off:

* **Local relief within `r comma(p$relief_radius_m / 1000)` km**: the highest minus the lowest DEM elevation within `r comma(p$relief_radius_m / 1000)` km of each event. Steep, deeply cut valleys funnel runoff; this measures that directly from the DEM.
* **County code** for joining FEMA's National Risk Index in Python.

```{r}
#| label: relief-5km
flood_events <- model_table |>
  dplyr::filter(is_flood_event == 1, !is.na(longitude))

relief_cache <- file.path(paths$derived_dir, sprintf("event_relief_%sm.parquet", p$relief_radius_m))
relief_sig <- digest::digest(list(sort(flood_events$event_id), p$relief_radius_m, file_signature(paths$dem)))
sig_file <- sub("\\.parquet$", ".sig", relief_cache)
relief <- if (file.exists(relief_cache) && file.exists(sig_file) && identical(readLines(sig_file), relief_sig)) {
  arrow::read_parquet(relief_cache)
} else {
  dem <- terra::rast(paths$dem)
  pts <- sf::st_as_sf(flood_events[c("event_id", "longitude", "latitude")],
                      coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = p$geographic_crs) |>
    clean_spatial_layer(p$analysis_crs)
  buffers <- terra::vect(sf::st_buffer(pts, p$relief_radius_m))
  hi <- terra::extract(dem, buffers, fun = max, na.rm = TRUE, ID = FALSE)[[1]]
  lo <- terra::extract(dem, buffers, fun = min, na.rm = TRUE, ID = FALSE)[[1]]
  out <- tibble::tibble(event_id = pts$event_id, local_relief_5km = hi - lo)
  arrow::write_parquet(out, relief_cache)
  writeLines(relief_sig, sub("\\.parquet$", ".sig", relief_cache))
  out
}

# Columns handed to Python (dates as text so both languages agree on them).
# Rainfall, hydrology, and tract SVI columns are passed only when the earlier
# sections produced them; Python skips any feature group that is missing.
# (mutate + select rather than transmute: transmute does not accept any_of().)
optional_ml_cols <- c("rain_event_total_mm", "rain_max_1day_mm", "rain_antecedent_7d_mm",
                      "hand_m", "log_drainage_area_km2",
                      "svi_rpl_themes", "svi_rpl_theme1", "svi_rpl_theme2", "svi_rpl_theme3", "svi_rpl_theme4")
flood_ml <- flood_events |>
  dplyr::left_join(relief, by = "event_id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    event_date = as.character(event_date),
    county_fips3 = suppressWarnings(as.integer(sub(";.*$", "", matched_county_fips)))
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    event_id, episode_id, event_date, event_year, event_month, split,
    latitude, longitude, region, in_study_area, cz_name, event_type, county_fips3,
    total_deaths, total_damage, high_consequence, is_tropical_event,
    slope_degrees, elevation_m, impervious_mean_250m, distance_to_stream_m, local_relief_5km,
    dplyr::any_of(optional_ml_cols)
  ) |>
  as.data.frame()
damage_threshold <- targets$threshold
```

The modeling code lives in `src/python/highground_ml.py` so it can be read, changed, and rerun on its own (`python src/python/highground_ml.py --project-dir .`). The chunks below call its functions in order.

```{python}
#| label: py-features
import os
import sys
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(r.project_dir, "src", "python"))
import highground_ml as hg

cfg = r.p
TARGET = hg.TARGET

# Adds county NRI values (population density, SOVI_SCORE), local flood history
# (earlier minor and severe floods within 25 km in the past 3 years; only past
# events count), the Aug-Oct season flag, and one-hot region columns.
df = hg.build_model_frame(r.flood_ml, r.paths["nri"],
                          history_radius_km=cfg["history_radius_km"],
                          history_window_years=cfg["history_window_years"])
devel, test = hg.split_frame(df)

# Feature groups, from season alone up to every group present in the data.
# The primary model uses the largest group that is available.
rungs = hg.resolve_ladder(devel)
FEATURES, primary_rung = hg.primary_features(rungs)

availability = hg.feature_availability(df, FEATURES)
summary = {
    "devel_n": len(devel), "devel_pos": int(devel[TARGET].sum()),
    "test_n": len(test), "test_pos": int(test[TARGET].sum()),
    "primary_rung": primary_rung, "n_features": len(FEATURES),
}
```

The models use **`r comma(py$summary$devel_n)` flood events from `r p$start_year`-`r p$validation_end_year`** for development (`r py$summary$devel_pos` high-consequence) and hold out **`r comma(py$summary$test_n)` events from `r p$validation_end_year + 1`-`r p$end_year`** (`r py$summary$test_pos` high-consequence) as a final test. The target is `high_consequence` with the damage threshold learned from training years only (`r scales::dollar(damage_threshold)`). The primary model uses the **`r py$summary$n_features` features** above (feature set "`r py$summary$primary_rung`" in the comparison below).

## Three models, three trade-offs

| Model | How it works | Strength | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Logistic regression** | One weight per feature, summed into a probability | Every weight can be read and explained | Assumes each feature acts on its own, along a straight line |
| **Random forest** | 100 decision trees on random subsets of events and features; their votes are averaged | Captures combinations (e.g. steep *and* rural) | Harder to explain a single prediction |
| **Histogram gradient boosting** | Trees built one after another, each correcting the last | Often the most accurate | The least transparent; reported for comparison |

How we trained them:

1. **Leakage-safe labels**: the damage threshold comes from training years only.
2. **Class weights** (`class_weight="balanced"`): only about 5% of events are high-consequence, so without weighting a model can just predict "safe" every time.
3. **Grouped cross-validation**: folds are grouped by `episode_id`, so events from one storm never sit on both sides of a split.
4. **Median imputation fit inside each fold**, so missing values are filled using training rows only.
5. **Calibration**: Platt scaling fit on *out-of-fold* predictions, so predicted probabilities can be read as real chances.

```{python}
#| label: py-cv
# One fixed set of grouped folds (seeds 100 + repeat), reused for every model
# and every feature set so that scores can be compared fold by fold.
folds = hg.make_group_folds(devel[TARGET], devel["episode_id"],
                            repeats=int(cfg["cv_repeats"]), folds=int(cfg["cv_folds"]))
cv_cache = {}   # fold scores shared between the model comparison and the ladder
cv_results, cv_fold_scores = hg.compare_models(devel, FEATURES, folds, cache=cv_cache)
best_cv = hg.best_model(cv_results)

# Feature ladder: random forest and logistic regression on growing feature sets
ladder, ladder_fold_scores = hg.feature_ladder(devel, folds, rungs, cache=cv_cache)
```

## Cross-validated performance

```{r}
#| label: cv-table
#| echo: false
py$cv_results |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `PR-AUC` = ifelse(is.na(pr_auc_sd), sprintf("%.3f", pr_auc), sprintf("%.3f +/- %.3f", pr_auc, pr_auc_sd)),
    `ROC-AUC` = ifelse(is.na(roc_auc_sd), sprintf("%.3f", roc_auc), sprintf("%.3f +/- %.3f", roc_auc, roc_auc_sd)),
    `Lift over baseline (PR-AUC)` = ifelse(model == "No-skill baseline", "", sprintf("%.1fx", pr_auc / pr_auc[model == "No-skill baseline"]))
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(Model = model, `PR-AUC`, `ROC-AUC`, `Lift over baseline (PR-AUC)`) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf("Repeated grouped cross-validation (%s x %s folds) on %s-%s flood events; mean +/- SD across folds",
                                 p$cv_repeats, p$cv_folds, p$start_year, p$validation_end_year))
```

```{r}
#| label: cv-numbers
#| include: false
# Numbers quoted in the text, looked up by model and feature-set name
fmt3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
fmt_pct <- function(x) scales::percent(x, accuracy = 1)
cvr <- py$cv_results
cv_base <- cvr$pr_auc[cvr$model == "No-skill baseline"]
cv_best <- cvr[cvr$model == py$best_cv$model, ]
lad <- py$ladder
# The ladder runs the random forest and logistic regression; quote the best
# cross-validated model if it is one of them, otherwise the random forest.
lad_model <- if (py$best_cv$model %in% lad$model) py$best_cv$model else "Random forest"
lad_row <- function(rung, model = lad_model) lad[lad$rung == rung & lad$model == model, ]
rung_ok <- function(rung) any(lad$rung == rung & lad$status == "evaluated")
gain_text <- function(rung, model = lad_model, vs = "season") {
  r <- lad_row(rung, model)
  if (nrow(r) == 0 || is.na(r[[paste0("pr_gain_vs_", vs)]])) return("not available in this run")
  g <- r[[paste0("pr_gain_vs_", vs)]]
  lo <- r[[paste0("pr_gain_vs_", vs, "_lo")]]
  hi <- r[[paste0("pr_gain_vs_", vs, "_hi")]]
  verdict <- if (lo <= 0 && hi >= 0) {
    "the interval includes zero, so the data do not show a reliable gain"
  } else if (hi < 0) {
    "a reliable loss"
  } else if (g < 0.05) {
    "small, but positive across the interval"
  } else {
    "positive across the interval"
  }
  sprintf("%+.3f (approximate 95%% interval %+.3f to %+.3f; %s)", g, lo, hi, verdict)
}
season_row <- lad_row("Season only")
primary_row <- lad_row(py$summary$primary_rung)
primary_reading <- with(primary_row, if (pr_gain_vs_season_lo <= 0) {
  "the surroundings of an event do not add a gain we can distinguish from zero beyond knowing when it happened"
} else if (pr_gain_vs_season < 0.05) {
  "the surroundings of an event add a real but small amount beyond knowing when it happened"
} else {
  "the surroundings of an event add clearly beyond knowing when it happened"
})
```

**PR-AUC is the number that matters here.** High-consequence events are rare, so a model can post a respectable ROC-AUC while still being poor at ranking the few events that matter. A model that guesses at random scores the share of positives, **`r fmt3(cv_base)`**. The best model, **`r py$best_cv$model`**, reaches **`r fmt3(cv_best$pr_auc)` ± `r fmt3(cv_best$pr_auc_sd)`** (mean ± SD across `r cv_best$n_folds` folds; `r sprintf("%.1f", cv_best$pr_auc / cv_base)`x the base rate). That is a modest score in absolute terms: most events the model ranks highest are still not high-consequence. A `r tolower(lad_model)` that sees only the season (event month and the August-October flag) already reaches **`r fmt3(season_row$pr_auc)`**, so much of the signal is timing. The spread across folds is wide because each fold holds only a handful of positive events.

## What each feature group adds

Season alone carries a lot of the signal, so the fair question is how much each group of features adds **on top of season**. We refit the random forest and the logistic regression on a ladder of feature sets, adding one group at a time, and scored every set on the **same** cross-validation folds. That lets us compare them fold by fold: for each fold, the PR-AUC of a feature set minus the PR-AUC of "Season only". "Region only" (mountains, central, coastal) is a side comparison and is not carried into later rows. Feature groups whose columns are not in the data yet are listed as skipped.

```{r}
#| label: ladder-table
#| echo: false
ladder_show <- lad |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `PR-AUC` = ifelse(is.na(pr_auc), "", sprintf("%.3f +/- %.3f", pr_auc, pr_auc_sd)),
    `ROC-AUC` = ifelse(is.na(roc_auc), "", sprintf("%.3f +/- %.3f", roc_auc, roc_auc_sd)),
    `Gain vs season (95% interval)` = ifelse(is.na(pr_gain_vs_season), "",
      sprintf("%+.3f (%+.3f to %+.3f)", pr_gain_vs_season, pr_gain_vs_season_lo, pr_gain_vs_season_hi)),
    `Folds beating season` = ifelse(is.na(share_folds_beat_season), "", scales::percent(share_folds_beat_season, accuracy = 1)),
    `Gain vs previous row (95% interval)` = ifelse(is.na(pr_gain_vs_previous), "",
      sprintf("%+.3f (%+.3f to %+.3f)", pr_gain_vs_previous, pr_gain_vs_previous_lo, pr_gain_vs_previous_hi))
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(`Feature set` = rung, Model = model, `Features added` = features_added, Status = status,
                `N features` = n_features, `PR-AUC`, `ROC-AUC`, `Gain vs season (95% interval)`,
                `Folds beating season`, `Gain vs previous row (95% interval)`)
dt(ladder_show, name = "model_feature_ladder", page_length = nrow(ladder_show),
   caption = sprintf("PR-AUC mean +/- SD over %s x %s grouped folds (base rate %.3f). Gains are paired fold-wise differences; intervals are mean +/- 1.96 SD / sqrt(folds), approximate because folds share data.",
                     p$cv_repeats, p$cv_folds, cv_base))
```

```{python}
#| label: py-ladder-plot

import matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.rcParams.update({"font.family": "sans-serif", "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False})
colors = {"Logistic regression": "#1b7a8c", "Random forest": "#b2182b", "Gradient boosting": "#e08e2b"}
done = ladder[ladder["status"] == "evaluated"]
order = list(dict.fromkeys(done["rung"]))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5.5))
for k, (name, g) in enumerate(done.groupby("model", sort=False)):
    g = g.set_index("rung").loc[order]
    x = np.arange(len(order)) + (k - 0.5) * 0.18
    ax.errorbar(x, g["pr_auc"], yerr=g["pr_auc_sd"], fmt="o", color=colors[name], capsize=3,
                linewidth=1.4, label=f"{name} (mean +/- SD across folds)")
    ax.axhline(g.loc["Season only", "pr_auc"], color=colors[name], linestyle=":", linewidth=1.2)
ax.axhline(float(ladder["base_rate"].iloc[0]), color="gray", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.2,
           label=f"No-skill base rate ({float(ladder['base_rate'].iloc[0]):.3f})")
ax.plot([], [], color="black", linestyle=":", label="Season-only score (dotted, per model)")
ax.set_xticks(np.arange(len(order)), order, rotation=20, ha="right")
ax.set_ylabel("Cross-validated PR-AUC")
ax.set_ylim(0, None)
ax.set_title("What each feature group adds over season alone", loc="left", fontweight="bold", color="#12344d")
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9, loc="lower right")
ax.grid(alpha=0.25, axis="y")
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(f"{r.paths['figures_dir']}/22_model_feature_ladder.png", dpi=int(cfg["figure_dpi"]), bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()
```

```{r}
lc1 <- function(x) paste0(tolower(substr(x, 1, 1)), substr(x, 2, nchar(x)))   # lowercase first letter only, keep acronyms
group_label <- c(`+ Place` = "Place (terrain, streams, paved surface)", `+ People` = "People (county SOVI, population density)",
                 `+ History` = "Local flood history", `+ Rainfall` = "Rainfall", `+ Hydrology` = "Hydrology (HAND, drainage area)",
                 `+ Tract SVI` = "Tract-level SVI")
steps <- lad |> dplyr::filter(status == "evaluated", !is.na(pr_gain_vs_previous))
cat("**Gain from each group over the row before it** (cross-validated PR-AUC, approximate 95% interval; **bold** = interval above zero):\n\n")
for (m in unique(steps$model)) {
  sm <- dplyr::filter(steps, model == m)
  parts <- sprintf(ifelse(sm$pr_gain_vs_previous_lo > 0, "**%s %+.3f (%+.3f to %+.3f)**", "%s %+.3f (%+.3f to %+.3f)"),
                   unname(group_label[sm$rung]), sm$pr_gain_vs_previous, sm$pr_gain_vs_previous_lo, sm$pr_gain_vs_previous_hi)
  cat(sprintf("* %s: %s.\n", m, paste(parts, collapse = "; ")))
}
clear <- dplyr::filter(steps, pr_gain_vs_previous_lo > 0)
cat("\n")
for (m in unique(steps$model)) {
  cm <- dplyr::filter(clear, model == m)
  full <- dplyr::filter(lad, model == m, rung == py$summary$primary_rung)
  cat(sprintf("For the %s, the groups that clearly add value are: %s. With all %s features it reaches %s, a gain of %s over season alone.\n\n",
              tolower(m),
              if (nrow(cm) == 0) "none" else paste(lc1(unname(group_label[cm$rung])), collapse = ", "),
              py$summary$n_features, fmt3(full$pr_auc), gain_text(py$summary$primary_rung, model = m)))
}
cat(sprintf("Region alone scores %s, close to the base rate. These intervals treat folds as independent, which they are not (repeats reuse the same events), so they are likely somewhat too narrow.\n",
            fmt3(lad_row("Region only")$pr_auc)))
```

## Holdout test (`r p$validation_end_year + 1`-`r p$end_year`)

```{python}
#| label: py-final-fit
# Fit on all development years; Platt scaling is fit on 5-fold out-of-fold
# predictions within those years (see the calibration section).
fit = hg.fit_holdout(devel, test, FEATURES)
fitted, preds, holdout = fit["fitted"], fit["preds"], fit["holdout"]
X_test_i, y_test, test_base_rate = fit["X_test_i"], fit["y_test"], fit["test_base_rate"]

# Calibration check (the "in-bag" bug): Platt scaling fit on the random
# forest's own training predictions instead of out-of-fold predictions.
calib_compare = hg.calibration_check(fit, "Random forest")

# Uncertainty: resample whole storm episodes (2,000 times) and recompute every
# metric, because events from one storm are not independent.
holdout_ci = hg.holdout_bootstrap(fit, test, n_boot=2000, seed=2026)
```

```{r}
#| label: holdout-numbers
#| include: false
hci <- py$holdout_ci
ci_row <- function(model, metric) hci[hci$model == model & hci$metric == metric, ]
ci_text <- function(model, metric, fmt = fmt3) {
  r <- ci_row(model, metric)
  sprintf("%s (95%% CI %s to %s)", fmt(r$estimate), fmt(r$lo), fmt(r$hi))
}
best_ho <- py$holdout$model[which.max(py$holdout$pr_auc)]
```

```{r}
#| label: holdout-table
#| echo: false
ci_cell <- function(model, metric, fmt) {
  r <- ci_row(model, metric)
  sprintf("%s (%s-%s)", fmt(r$estimate), fmt(r$lo), fmt(r$hi))
}
tibble::tibble(Model = py$holdout$model) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `PR-AUC` = purrr::map_chr(Model, ci_cell, metric = "pr_auc", fmt = fmt3),
    `ROC-AUC` = purrr::map_chr(Model, ci_cell, metric = "roc_auc", fmt = fmt3),
    `Top 10%: share of positives caught` = purrr::map_chr(Model, ci_cell, metric = "top10_capture", fmt = fmt_pct),
    `Top 10%: precision` = purrr::map_chr(Model, ci_cell, metric = "top10_precision", fmt = fmt_pct),
    `Top 20%: share of positives caught` = purrr::map_chr(Model, ci_cell, metric = "top20_capture", fmt = fmt_pct),
    `Mean predicted risk` = scales::percent(py$holdout$mean_predicted, accuracy = 0.1)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf("Holdout test on %s events (%s high-consequence, base rate %s). Brackets: 95%% cluster-bootstrap interval, resampling storm episodes (%s resamples).",
                                 comma(py$summary$test_n), py$summary$test_pos, scales::percent(py$test_base_rate, accuracy = 0.1),
                                 comma(max(hci$n_boot_used))))
```

The holdout is one set of `r py$summary$test_pos` positives, mostly from a few storms, so its intervals are wide. The `r tolower(py$best_cv$model)` (best in cross-validation) puts `r ci_text(py$best_cv$model, "top10_capture", fmt_pct)` of the test-year high-consequence events in its top 10% of predicted risk. `r if (identical(best_ho, py$best_cv$model)) sprintf("It also has the highest holdout PR-AUC (%s).", ci_text(best_ho, "pr_auc")) else sprintf("The %s does best on this holdout (PR-AUC %s; top 10%% catches %s).", tolower(best_ho), ci_text(best_ho, "pr_auc"), ci_text(best_ho, "top10_capture", fmt_pct))` The intervals for the models overlap, so this holdout cannot say which model is better.

```{python}
#| label: py-helene

```

```{r}
hs_val <- function(model, subset, col) hs[[col]][hs$model == model & hs$subset == subset]
hs |>
  dplyr::mutate(subset = dplyr::recode(subset, "Excluding window" = paste("Excluding", p$highlight_event_name, "week"),
                                       "Window only" = paste(p$highlight_event_name, "week only")),

  dplyr::select(Model = model, `Test events` = subset, Events = n_events, `High-consequence` = n_positive,
```

**`r p$highlight_event_name` dominates the test years.** `r fmt_pct(hs$share_test_positives_in_window[1])` of the test-year high-consequence events fall in the `r p$highlight_event_name` week (`r p$highlight_start_date` to `r p$highlight_end_date`). Without that week, the test set has `r hs_val(best_ho, "Excluding window", "n_positive")` positives (base rate `r scales::percent(hs_val(best_ho, "Excluding window", "base_rate"), accuracy = 0.1)`), and the `r tolower(best_ho)`'s PR-AUC falls from `r fmt3(hs_val(best_ho, "All test events", "pr_auc"))` to `r fmt3(hs_val(best_ho, "Excluding window", "pr_auc"))` (ROC-AUC `r fmt3(hs_val(best_ho, "Excluding window", "roc_auc"))`)`r if (!identical(best_ho, py$best_cv$model)) sprintf("; the %s scores %s", tolower(py$best_cv$model), fmt3(hs_val(py$best_cv$model, "Excluding window", "pr_auc"))) else ""`. `r if (hs$share_test_positives_in_window[1] > 0.5) "Most" else "Part"` of the holdout score therefore measures how well the models recognize one storm.

## Does it generalize?

The scores above come from folds that hold out whole storms, and from one holdout dominated by one storm. That is not enough to say the model works on places and years it has not seen. This section runs five harder checks. All of them use the same features and the same model settings as above; the code is in `src/python/highground_ml.py`.

```{python}
#| label: py-generalize
# 1. Ablation: the full model minus each feature group, and two small subsets,
#    scored on the same 5 x 5 episode-grouped folds as the ladder.
ablation = hg.ablation_study(devel, folds, FEATURES, cache=cv_cache)
# 2. Spatial: hold out whole counties (10 folds, same repeat seeds) or a whole
#    region, development years only. "Storm-purged" also drops training events
#    from any storm that reached the held-out place.
spatial_cv, spatial_cv_folds = hg.spatial_validation(devel, FEATURES, folds, repeats=int(cfg["cv_repeats"]),
                                                     county_folds=10, cache=cv_cache)
storm_span = hg.storm_span_summary(devel, spatial_cv_folds)
# 3. Temporal: for each year Y, fit on every earlier year and score year Y.
temporal = hg.rolling_origin(df, FEATURES, first_year=int(cfg["start_year"]) + 3,
                             last_year=int(cfg["end_year"]) - 1, min_pos=5)
# 4. Label-permutation test (500 shuffles of the development labels, one
#    repeat of 5-fold episode-grouped CV). Shuffles single events, which
#    ignores storm structure.
permutation = hg.permutation_test(devel, FEATURES, model="Logistic regression", n_perm=500)
# 5. Reliability by risk decile from out-of-fold predictions (first CV repeat).
calib_deciles = hg.calibration_deciles(devel, FEATURES, folds, model="Logistic regression")
```

```{r}
#| label: generalize-numbers
#| include: false
# Every number quoted in this subsection comes from these lookups.
gen_model <- if (py$best_cv$model %in% py$spatial_cv$model) py$best_cv$model else "Logistic regression"
other_model <- setdiff(unique(py$spatial_cv$model), gen_model)[1]
p_text <- function(x) if (x < 0.001) "p < 0.001" else sprintf("p = %.3f", x)
and_list <- function(x) if (length(x) <= 1) paste(x) else paste(paste(head(x, -1), collapse = ", "), "and", tail(x, 1))

# Ablation
abl <- py$ablation
abl_row <- function(set, model = gen_model) abl[abl$set == set & abl$model == model, ]
abl_gain <- function(set, model = gen_model) {
  r <- abl_row(set, model)
  if (nrow(r) == 0) return("not available in this run")
  sprintf("%+.3f (approximate 95%% interval %+.3f to %+.3f)", r$gain_full_vs_set, r$gain_lo, r$gain_hi)
}
abl_drop <- abl[abl$model == gen_model & abl$kind == "drop one", ]
abl_drop$group <- sub("^Full minus ", "", abl_drop$set)
abl_needed <- abl_drop$group[abl_drop$gain_lo > 0]
abl_spare <- abl_drop$group[abl_drop$gain_lo <= 0]
abl_top <- abl_drop[which.max(abl_drop$gain_full_vs_set), ]
ladder_clear <- sub("^\\+ ", "", lad$rung[lad$model == gen_model & lad$status == "evaluated" &
                                          !is.na(lad$pr_gain_vs_previous_lo) & lad$pr_gain_vs_previous_lo > 0])
ladder_clear <- intersect(ladder_clear, abl_drop$group)
only_ablation <- setdiff(abl_needed, c(ladder_clear, "Season"))   # Season is the ladder's base, never "added"
only_ladder <- setdiff(ladder_clear, abl_needed)
list_or_none <- function(x) if (length(x) == 0) "none" else and_list(x)
abl_reading <- if (length(only_ablation) == 0 && length(only_ladder) == 0) {
  "The ablation agrees with the ladder, so the order in which groups were added does not change the story."
} else {
  one_a <- length(only_ablation) == 1; one_l <- length(only_ladder) == 1
  paste0("The order of the ladder matters. ",
         if (length(only_ablation) > 0) sprintf("%s did not clearly add when entering the ladder, but removing %s from the full model costs PR-AUC: %s only in combination with other groups. ",
                                                and_list(only_ablation), if (one_a) "it" else "them", if (one_a) "it helps" else "they help") else "",
         if (length(only_ladder) > 0) sprintf("%s clearly added in the ladder, but the full model does not reliably need %s once every other group is in: what %s overlaps with other groups. ",
                                              and_list(only_ladder), if (one_l) "it" else "them", if (one_l) "it carries" else "they carry") else "")
}

# Spatial
sp <- py$spatial_cv
sp_val <- function(scheme, held = NULL, model = gen_model, col = "pr_auc") {
  r <- sp[sp$scheme == scheme & sp$model == model, ]
  if (!is.null(held)) r <- r[r$held_out == held, ]
  if (nrow(r) == 0) NA_real_ else r[[col]][1]
}
ep_pr   <- sp_val("Episode-grouped CV")
cb_pr   <- sp_val("County-blocked CV")
cbp_pr  <- sp_val("County-blocked CV, storm-purged")
rg_pr   <- sp_val("Region held out", "Mean of regions")
rgp_pr  <- sp_val("Region held out, storm-purged", "Mean of regions")
place_cmp <- function(x) {
  ratio <- x / ep_pr
  if (is.na(ratio)) "could not be scored, so it cannot be compared with" else if (ratio < 0.8) "well below" else
    if (ratio < 0.95) "somewhat below" else if (ratio <= 1.05) "close to" else "above"
}
regions <- sp[sp$scheme == "Region held out" & sp$model == gen_model & sp$held_out != "Mean of regions", ]
region_list <- paste(sprintf("%s %s (base rate %s)", regions$held_out,
                             ifelse(is.na(regions$pr_auc), "not scored: no positives", fmt3(regions$pr_auc)),
                             fmt3(regions$base_rate)), collapse = "; ")
regions_nan <- regions$held_out[is.na(regions$pr_auc)]
county_nan <- sp$n_folds_no_pos[sp$scheme == "County-blocked CV" & sp$model == gen_model]
county_k <- sp_val("County-blocked CV", col = "n_folds") / p$cv_repeats
mtn <- regions[regions$held_out == "mountains", ]
mtn_other <- sp[sp$scheme == "Region held out" & sp$model == other_model & sp$held_out == "mountains", ]
place_leans <- any(c(cbp_pr, rg_pr) / ep_pr < 0.8, na.rm = TRUE)
place_reading <- if (place_leans) {
  "The model leans on place-specific patterns: it ranks events noticeably less well in places it has never seen, so the episode-grouped score overstates how it would do in a new county or region."
} else if (any(c(cbp_pr, rg_pr) / ep_pr < 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)) {
  "Part of the score depends on having seen the place before, but most of it carries over to unseen counties and regions."
} else {
  "The score carries over to unseen counties and regions about as well as to unseen storms."
}

# Temporal
tm <- py$temporal
tm_years <- tm[tm$model == gen_model & !is.na(tm$year), ]
tm_pool <- tm[tm$model == gen_model & is.na(tm$year), ]
tm_ok <- tm_years[!tm_years$few_positives & !is.na(tm_years$pr_auc), ]
tm_few <- tm_years$year[tm_years$few_positives]
tm_near <- tm_years$year[!is.na(tm_years$pr_auc) & tm_years$pr_auc < 2 * tm_years$base_rate]
tm_lo <- tm_ok[which.min(tm_ok$pr_auc), ]
tm_hi <- tm_ok[which.max(tm_ok$pr_auc), ]
hl_year <- as.integer(substr(p$highlight_start_date, 1, 4))
tm_reading <- paste0(
  if (nrow(tm_ok) >= 2 && tm_hi$pr_auc - tm_lo$pr_auc > 0.15) "Skill is uneven from year to year. " else
    if (nrow(tm_ok) >= 2) "Skill is fairly steady from year to year. " else "",
  if (nrow(tm_ok) >= 2 && tm_hi$positives == max(tm_ok$positives)) "The best year is also the year with the most high-consequence events." else "")

# Permutation
pm <- py$permutation
perm_reading <- if (pm$p_value <= 0.01) {
  sprintf("%s of the %s shuffles reached the observed score (%s%s), so the signal is very unlikely to be chance.",
          if (pm$n_null_ge_observed == 0) "None" else comma(pm$n_null_ge_observed), comma(pm$n_perm), p_text(pm$p_value),
          if (pm$n_null_ge_observed == 0) ", the smallest value this many shuffles can give" else "")
} else if (pm$p_value <= 0.05) {
  sprintf("%s of the %s shuffles reached the observed score (%s). That is small, but not overwhelming.",
          comma(pm$n_null_ge_observed), comma(pm$n_perm), p_text(pm$p_value))
} else {
  sprintf("%s of the %s shuffles reached the observed score (%s). That p-value is not small: the cross-validated score cannot be told apart from what shuffled labels produce.",
          comma(pm$n_null_ge_observed), comma(pm$n_perm), p_text(pm$p_value))
}

# Reliability deciles
cd <- py$calib_deciles
cd_gap <- max(abs(cd$observed_rate - cd$mean_predicted))
cd_worst <- cd[which.max(abs(cd$observed_rate - cd$mean_predicted)), ]
cd_top <- cd[cd$decile == max(cd$decile), ]
cd_bot <- cd[cd$decile == min(cd$decile), ]
cd_worst_text <- sprintf("decile %s: %s predicted, %s observed", cd_worst$decile,
                         scales::percent(cd_worst$mean_predicted, accuracy = 0.1), scales::percent(cd_worst$observed_rate, accuracy = 0.1))
cd_reading <- if (cd_gap < 0.02) {
  sprintf("Predicted and observed rates stay within %.1f percentage points in every decile (largest gap in %s), so within the development years the calibrated probabilities can be read as chances.", 100 * cd_gap, cd_worst_text)
} else if (cd_gap < 0.05) {
  cd_se2 <- 2 * sqrt(cd_worst$mean_predicted * (1 - cd_worst$mean_predicted) / cd_worst$n)   # 2 binomial SEs
  sprintf("Predicted and observed rates roughly match; the largest gap is %.1f percentage points (%s), %s two binomial standard errors (%.1f points) for a decile of %s events. Read the probabilities as approximate.",
          100 * cd_gap, cd_worst_text, if (cd_gap <= cd_se2) "within" else "beyond", 100 * cd_se2, comma(cd_worst$n))
} else {
  sprintf("Predicted and observed rates differ by up to %.1f percentage points (%s), so the probabilities should not be read as exact chances.", 100 * cd_gap, cd_worst_text)
}
```

### Is the ladder order flattering a group?

The ladder adds feature groups in one fixed order, so a group that enters early can take credit that a later group would also have earned, and a group that only helps in combination can look useless. Here we instead remove one group at a time from the full model, and also fit two small models (rainfall only, and season plus rainfall). Each row is scored on the same folds as the ladder; the gain is the full model's PR-AUC minus the reduced model's, fold by fold. A gain whose interval is above zero means the full model needs that group even with every other group present.

```{r}
#| label: ablation-table
#| echo: false
abl_show <- abl |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(pr_auc, pr_auc_sd, roc_auc, full_pr_auc, gain_full_vs_set, gain_lo, gain_hi,
                                share_folds_full_better), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::select(set, kind, model, n_features, pr_auc, pr_auc_sd, roc_auc, full_pr_auc, gain_full_vs_set,
                gain_lo, gain_hi, share_folds_full_better, n_folds, features)
dt(abl_show, name = "model_ablation", page_length = nrow(abl_show),
   caption = sprintf("PR-AUC mean and SD over the same %s x %s episode-grouped folds as the ladder. gain_full_vs_set = full model minus this set, paired by fold; gain_lo/gain_hi = mean +/- 1.96 SD / sqrt(folds), approximate because folds share data.",
                     p$cv_repeats, p$cv_folds))
```

For the `r tolower(gen_model)`, rainfall alone reaches **`r fmt3(abl_row("Rainfall only")$pr_auc)`**, and the full model beats it by `r abl_gain("Rainfall only")`. Season plus rainfall reaches `r fmt3(abl_row("Season + Rainfall")$pr_auc)`. Removing one group at a time, the groups the full model clearly needs are: **`r list_or_none(abl_needed)`**. Removing `r list_or_none(abl_spare)` does not reliably change the score. Removing `r tolower(abl_top$group)` costs the most: `r abl_gain(abl_top$set)`. `r abl_reading`

### Does it work in places it has not seen?

Episode-grouped folds keep each storm on one side of the split, but the same counties appear in training and validation. Two stricter checks hold out **place** instead. *County-blocked* cross-validation holds out whole counties (`r county_k` folds of counties, repeated `r p$cv_repeats` times). *Region held out* trains on two of the three regions (mountains, central, coastal) and tests on the third. Both use only `r p$start_year`-`r p$validation_end_year`. Storms cross county lines: `r fmt_pct(py$storm_span$share_pos_multi_county)` of the development high-consequence events belong to a storm episode that reached more than one county, and `r fmt_pct(py$storm_span$share_pos_multi_region)` to one that reached more than one region. So we run each check twice: as is, and *storm-purged*, where training also drops every event from a storm that reached the held-out place.

```{r}
#| label: spatial-table
#| echo: false
sp_show <- sp |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(base_rate, pr_auc, pr_sd, roc_auc), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::select(scheme, model, held_out, n, positives, base_rate, pr_auc, pr_sd, roc_auc, n_folds, n_folds_no_pos)
dt(sp_show, name = "model_spatial_cv", page_length = nrow(sp_show),
   caption = "Development years only. CV rows: mean and SD of PR-AUC across folds. Region rows: one score per held-out region; read each against that region's base rate. n_folds_no_pos = folds or regions with no high-consequence events, recorded as missing.")
```

For the `r tolower(gen_model)`, episode-grouped cross-validation scores **`r fmt3(ep_pr)`**. Holding out whole counties and purging their storms from training, it scores **`r fmt3(cbp_pr)`**, `r place_cmp(cbp_pr)` the episode-grouped score. Without the purge the county-blocked score is `r fmt3(cb_pr)``r if (!is.na(cb_pr) && cb_pr > ep_pr) ", higher than episode-grouped, because a storm that crossed county lines then sits partly in training; that version flatters the model and we do not rely on it" else ""`. The purge also shrinks training, from about `r comma(round(py$storm_span$mean_train_unpurged))` to `r comma(round(py$storm_span$mean_train_purged))` events per fold, so part of any drop is less data. Holding out a whole region gives a mean of **`r fmt3(rg_pr)`** across the `r nrow(regions)` regions (`r fmt3(rgp_pr)` storm-purged), `r place_cmp(rg_pr)` the episode-grouped score: `r region_list`. `r if (nrow(mtn) == 1 && !is.na(mtn$pr_auc)) sprintf("For the mountains, the region this project is about, a model that never saw a mountain event scores %s against a base rate of %s (%.1fx); the %s scores %s.", fmt3(mtn$pr_auc), fmt3(mtn$base_rate), mtn$pr_auc / mtn$base_rate, tolower(other_model), fmt3(mtn_other$pr_auc)) else ""` `r if (length(regions_nan) > 0) sprintf("No score is possible for %s: the held-out region has no high-consequence events.", and_list(regions_nan)) else ""``r if (isTRUE(county_nan > 0)) sprintf(" %s county folds had no high-consequence events and are left out of the county-blocked mean.", county_nan) else ""` `r place_reading`

### Does it work in years it has not seen?

The holdout is one block of years. A *rolling-origin* check asks the same question year by year: for each year from `r min(tm_years$year)` to `r max(tm_years$year)`, fit on every earlier year (`r p$start_year` onward) and score that year only. The target is used exactly as exported; its damage threshold is not recomputed.

```{r}
#| label: temporal-table
#| echo: false
tm_show <- tm |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(base_rate, pr_auc, roc_auc), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::select(label, year, model, n_train, train_positives, n, positives, base_rate, pr_auc, roc_auc, few_positives)
dt(tm_show, name = "model_temporal", page_length = nrow(tm_show),
   caption = sprintf("Each year is scored by a model fit on all earlier years. few_positives = TRUE when the year has fewer than %s high-consequence events, so its score rests on a handful of events. The pooled row scores all test years together.", tm_years$min_pos[1]))
```

Across the years with at least `r tm_years$min_pos[1]` high-consequence events, the `r tolower(gen_model)`'s PR-AUC ranges from **`r fmt3(tm_lo$pr_auc)` (`r tm_lo$year`, base rate `r fmt3(tm_lo$base_rate)`)** to **`r fmt3(tm_hi$pr_auc)` (`r tm_hi$year`, base rate `r fmt3(tm_hi$base_rate)`)**`r if (identical(as.integer(tm_hi$year), hl_year)) sprintf(", the %s year", p$highlight_event_name) else ""`. Pooled over all years it scores `r fmt3(tm_pool$pr_auc)` against a base rate of `r fmt3(tm_pool$base_rate)` (a rough summary: each year's predictions come from a different fit). `r if (length(tm_near) == 0) "No year scores below twice its base rate." else sprintf("Years where it scores less than twice that year's base rate, close to guessing: %s.", and_list(tm_near))` `r if (length(tm_few) > 0) sprintf("%s had fewer than %s high-consequence events, so %s say%s little either way.", and_list(tm_few), tm_years$min_pos[1], if (length(tm_few) == 1) "its score" else "their scores", if (length(tm_few) == 1) "s" else "") else ""` `r tm_reading`

### Could a score this high happen by chance?

We shuffled the development labels `r comma(pm$n_perm)` times, refit the `r tolower(pm$model)` on each shuffle, and scored it with one repeat of `r pm$n_folds`-fold episode-grouped cross-validation. On the real labels that same single repeat scores **`r fmt3(pm$observed)`** (one repeat, so it differs from the `r p$cv_repeats`-repeat mean above). The shuffled labels average `r fmt3(pm$null_mean)` and their 95th percentile is `r fmt3(pm$null_p95)`. `r perm_reading` The shuffle moves single events, not whole storms, so the shuffled scores are probably somewhat too tightly bunched. `r if (pm$observed > pm$null_max) sprintf("The real score is above even the highest shuffled score (%s), so a wider null is unlikely to change the conclusion.", fmt3(pm$null_max)) else "Treat the p-value as a lower bound."`

```{r}
#| label: permutation-table
#| echo: false
pm_show <- pm |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(observed, null_mean, null_sd, null_p95, null_max, p_value), \(x) round(x, 4)))
dt(pm_show, name = "model_permutation", page_length = 1)
```

### Do predicted risks match observed rates?

Using the out-of-fold predictions of the `r tolower(gen_model)` (each development event scored by a model that did not see its storm), we split events into `r nrow(cd)` equal groups by predicted risk and compare the mean prediction with the observed share of high-consequence events. Platt scaling is cross-fit: the scaling used on each fold is learned from the other folds.

```{r}
#| label: calib-deciles-table
#| echo: false
cd_show <- cd |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(mean_predicted, observed_rate, mean_raw, min_predicted, max_predicted), \(x) round(x, 4)))
dt(cd_show, name = "model_calibration_deciles", page_length = nrow(cd_show))
```

The highest-risk group predicts `r scales::percent(cd_top$mean_predicted, accuracy = 0.1)` and observes `r scales::percent(cd_top$observed_rate, accuracy = 0.1)`, and holds `r fmt_pct(cd_top$positives / sum(cd$positives))` of all development high-consequence events. The lowest-risk group predicts `r scales::percent(cd_bot$mean_predicted, accuracy = 0.1)` and observes `r scales::percent(cd_bot$observed_rate, accuracy = 0.1)`. `r cd_reading`

```{python}
#| label: py-generalize-plot
#| results: hide
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.1, 1]})
# Left: PR-AUC by test year against that year's base rate
yrs = temporal[temporal["year"].notna()]
base = yrs.drop_duplicates("year")
ax1.bar(base["year"], base["base_rate"], width=0.6, color="#d9d9d9", label="Base rate of that year")
for k, (name, g) in enumerate(yrs.groupby("model", sort=False)):
    ax1.plot(g["year"], g["pr_auc"], "-", color=colors[name], linewidth=1.6)
    few = g["few_positives"].astype(bool)
    ax1.scatter(g.loc[~few, "year"], g.loc[~few, "pr_auc"], color=colors[name], s=40, zorder=3, label=name)
    ax1.scatter(g.loc[few, "year"], g.loc[few, "pr_auc"], facecolors="white", edgecolors=colors[name], s=40,
                zorder=3)
ax1.scatter([], [], facecolors="white", edgecolors="gray", s=40, label="Fewer than 5 positives that year")
ax1.set_xticks(base["year"], [str(int(v)) for v in base["year"]])
ax1.set_xlabel("Test year (model fit on all earlier years)")
ax1.set_ylabel("PR-AUC")
ax1.set_ylim(0, None)
ax1.set_title("Year by year (rolling origin)", loc="left", fontweight="bold", color="#12344d")
ax1.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8.5, loc="upper left")
ax1.grid(alpha=0.25, axis="y")
# Right: episode-grouped vs county-blocked vs region held out
schemes = [("Episode-grouped CV", "Episode-\ngrouped"), ("County-blocked CV", "County-\nblocked"),
           ("County-blocked CV, storm-purged", "County-blocked,\nstorm-purged"),
           ("Region held out", "Region\nheld out"), ("Region held out, storm-purged", "Region held out,\nstorm-purged")]
models_sp = list(dict.fromkeys(spatial_cv["model"]))
for k, name in enumerate(models_sp):
    s = spatial_cv[spatial_cv["model"] == name]
    off = (k - (len(models_sp) - 1) / 2) * 0.22
    for i, (sch, _) in enumerate(schemes):
        rows = s[s["scheme"] == sch]
        main = rows[rows["held_out"] == "Mean of regions"] if sch.startswith("Region") else rows
        if main.empty:
            continue
        sd = None if sch.startswith("Region") else main["pr_sd"].iloc[0]   # regions: ticks show the spread
        ax2.errorbar(i + off, main["pr_auc"].iloc[0], yerr=sd, fmt="o", color=colors[name],
                     capsize=3, markersize=7, label=name if i == 0 else None)
        if sch.startswith("Region"):
            reg = rows[rows["held_out"] != "Mean of regions"]
            ax2.scatter(np.full(len(reg), i + off), reg["pr_auc"], marker="_", s=120, color=colors[name], alpha=0.8)
dev_base = float(spatial_cv["base_rate"].iloc[0])
ax2.axhline(dev_base, color="gray", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.2, label=f"Development base rate ({dev_base:.3f})")
ax2.scatter([], [], marker="_", s=120, color="gray", label="Single held-out region")
ax2.set_xticks(range(len(schemes)), [lab for _, lab in schemes], fontsize=8.5)
ax2.set_ylabel("PR-AUC (CV: mean +/- SD; regions: mean and each region)")
ax2.set_ylim(0, None)
ax2.set_title("Unseen storms vs unseen places", loc="left", fontweight="bold", color="#12344d")
ax2.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8.5, loc="upper right")
ax2.grid(alpha=0.25, axis="y")
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(f"{r.paths['figures_dir']}/23_model_generalization.png", dpi=int(cfg["figure_dpi"]), bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()
```

## Are the probabilities trustworthy? Calibration

A model that says "10% risk" should be right about 10% of the time. Tree models are often poorly calibrated, so we rescale their scores with Platt scaling. **Where** that rescaling is fit matters. During development the team first fit it on the forest's own training predictions ("in-bag"). Those predictions are overconfident because the trees have already seen those rows, so the rescaling learned the wrong curve and pulled the average predicted risk below the observed rate. Fitting it on out-of-fold predictions corrects this:

```{r}
#| label: calib-table
#| echo: false
py$calib_compare |>
  dplyr::mutate(mean_predicted = scales::percent(mean_predicted, accuracy = 0.1),
                max_predicted = ifelse(is.na(max_predicted), "", scales::percent(max_predicted, accuracy = 0.1))) |>
  dplyr::rename(`Random forest calibration` = calibration, `Mean predicted risk (test)` = mean_predicted,
                `Highest predicted risk (test)` = max_predicted) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{python}
#| label: py-calibration
#| results: hide
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5
from sklearn.calibration import calibration_curve

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 5), sharey=True)
panels = [(preds["Random forest"]["raw"], "Random forest: raw scores"),
          (preds["Random forest"]["cal"], "Random forest: calibrated (out-of-fold Platt)")]
for ax, (probs, title) in zip(axes, panels):
    frac_pos, mean_pred = calibration_curve(y_test, probs, n_bins=8, strategy="quantile")
    ax.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], "k--", linewidth=1, label="Perfect calibration")
    ax.plot(mean_pred, frac_pos, "o-", color="#b2182b", linewidth=2, label="Model")
    ax.set_xlim(0, max(0.3, float(np.max(probs)) * 1.1))
    ax.set_ylim(0, max(0.3, float(np.max(frac_pos)) * 1.2))
    ax.set_title(title, loc="left", fontweight="bold", color="#12344d")
    ax.set_xlabel("Mean predicted probability")
    ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
axes[0].set_ylabel("Observed share high-consequence")
axes[0].legend(frameon=False)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(f"{r.paths['figures_dir']}/20_model_calibration.png", dpi=int(cfg["figure_dpi"]), bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
```



Each dot is one test event. Dots to the right pushed that event's predicted risk up, and color shows whether the feature's value was high (red) or low (blue). The table combines three views of each feature: its average influence in the random forest (mean |SHAP|), the direction of its effect in the logistic regression, and how many of the forest's 100 trees use it at all.

```{r}
#| label: driver-table
#| echo: false
drivers <- py$shap_importance |>
  dplyr::left_join(py$lr_coefs, by = "feature") |>
  dplyr::left_join(py$tree_use, by = "feature") |>
  dplyr::mutate(direction_in_logistic_model = ifelse(standardized_coefficient > 0, "raises risk", "lowers risk"),
                dplyr::across(c(mean_abs_shap, standardized_coefficient), \(x) round(x, 4)))
dt(drivers, name = "model_feature_drivers", page_length = nrow(drivers))
```

```{r}
#| label: driver-notes

dir_of <- function(f) drivers$direction_in_logistic_model[drivers$feature == f]
top3 <- paste(head(drivers$feature, 3), collapse = ", ")
cat(sprintf("* **Strongest drivers** (random forest): %s.\n", top3))
minor_dir <- dir_of("nearby_minor_flood_count_25km"); severe_dir <- dir_of("nearby_severe_flood_count_25km")
if (minor_dir != severe_dir) {
  cat(sprintf("* **Flood history cuts both ways:** more earlier *minor* floods nearby %s, while more earlier *severe* floods nearby %s. This is consistent with communities adapting after routine floods, while severe events cluster in the most exposed places.\n", minor_dir, severe_dir))
} else {
  cat(sprintf("* **Flood history:** both earlier minor and earlier severe floods nearby %s in this run.\n", sub("s risk$", " risk", minor_dir)))   # plural subject: "lower risk"
}
cat(sprintf("* **Paved surface** %s. A possible reason: urban flood reports are often minor, while the deadliest events hit rural, steep terrain. Differences in how urban and rural events get reported could also produce this pattern, and this analysis cannot tell the two apart.\n",
            dir_of("impervious_mean_250m")))
cat(sprintf("* **Season** (`peak_hurricane_season`) %s and is used by %s of 100 trees.\n",
            dir_of("peak_hurricane_season"), drivers$trees_using_feature[drivers$feature == "peak_hurricane_season"]))
```

## Lessons from development

Two problems turned up while the team built the models and the interactive explorer below. Both are recomputed here on this run's data.

```{python}
#| label: py-diagnostics
# 1. Refit the forest with the is_tropical_event flag added and count the trees that use it.
tropical_check = hg.tropical_flag_check(devel, FEATURES)
# 2. Score every mountain flood event as a July storm (outside the Aug-Oct peak)
#    and as a September storm (peak flag on), all else equal.
inversion = hg.season_inversion(fit, df, region="mountains", typical=(7, 0), hurricane=(9, 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: lessons-numbers
#| include: false
trop <- py$tropical_check
inv <- py$inversion
inv_val <- function(model, col) inv[[col]][inv$model == model]
cal <- py$calib_compare
cal_val <- function(row, col) cal[[col]][startsWith(cal$calibration, row)]
rf_inv <- inv_val("Random forest", "share_hurricane_lower")
lr_inv <- inv_val("Logistic regression", "share_hurricane_lower")
```

* **A flag the forest could not use.** An early version included an `is_tropical_event` flag that no tree in the random forest ever split on. Recomputed here, the flag equals 1 for `r trop$flag_events_devel` of the `r comma(py$summary$devel_n)` development flood events`r if (isTRUE(trop$flag_events_devel == 0)) ". It is constant: the flag is set from NOAA's event type, and no flood-type event in this table carries a tropical event type" else ""`. A forest refit with the flag added uses it in `r trop$trees_using_flag` of `r trop$n_trees` trees. The "hurricane versus ordinary storm" distinction therefore rests on the season features (`event_month` and `peak_hurricane_season`).
* **A mountain inversion.** We scored each of the `r comma(inv_val("Random forest", "n_events"))` mountain flood events twice, changing only the season: a July storm (outside the August-October peak) and a September storm (peak flag on). The calibrated random forest gives the September storm the **lower** risk for `r fmt_pct(rf_inv)` of these events (mean risk `r scales::percent(inv_val("Random forest", "mean_typical"), accuracy = 0.1)` for July versus `r scales::percent(inv_val("Random forest", "mean_hurricane"), accuracy = 0.1)` for September). The forest can do this because it learns month effects separately inside each terrain split, from few severe mountain examples. The logistic regression gives the lower risk for `r fmt_pct(lr_inv)` of events: its season effect is one fixed weight applied everywhere, so it moves every event in the same direction (mean `r scales::percent(inv_val("Logistic regression", "mean_typical"), accuracy = 0.1)` versus `r scales::percent(inv_val("Logistic regression", "mean_hurricane"), accuracy = 0.1)`). Earlier figures for this check came from the explorer's grid of mountain cells and an older model run; they are replaced by these.
* **The calibration bug.** Fitting Platt scaling on the forest's in-bag predictions distorts the risk scale. On this run's test years, the mean calibrated risk is `r scales::percent(cal_val("In-bag", "mean_predicted"), accuracy = 0.1)` with in-bag calibration and `r scales::percent(cal_val("Out-of-fold", "mean_predicted"), accuracy = 0.1)` with out-of-fold calibration, against an observed rate of `r scales::percent(py$test_base_rate, accuracy = 0.1)`. The highest single prediction is `r scales::percent(cal_val("In-bag", "max_predicted"), accuracy = 0.1)` versus `r scales::percent(cal_val("Out-of-fold", "max_predicted"), accuracy = 0.1)`. `r if (cal_val("In-bag", "max_predicted") > cal_val("Out-of-fold", "max_predicted") && cal_val("In-bag", "mean_predicted") < cal_val("Out-of-fold", "mean_predicted")) "The in-bag curve is not a uniform shrink: it pushes most events down and the top few up." else ""`

## Interactive risk explorer

The explorer is a browser tool for county planners, NCDOT staff, and researchers. It is rebuilt from this run's logistic regression (the same 14 inputs and calibration as the tables above). You can set a rainfall scenario and see the estimated chance that a flood-related event is high-consequence at each 5 km square, replay Hurricane Helene with its actual rainfall next to what NOAA recorded, click any place for a report card, and rank counties. Its validation tab repeats the checks in this section.

```{r}
#| label: explorer
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
# Rebuild the explorer from this run: R builds the map grid (cached), then
# src/python/export_explorer.py fits the model and writes the single-file page.
explorer_script <- file.path(project_dir, "src", "python", "export_explorer.py")
explorer_r <- file.path(project_dir, "src", "R", "explorer_data.R")
if (isTRUE(p$embed_explorer) && file.exists(explorer_script)) {
  grid_ok <- tryCatch({ source(explorer_r); build_explorer_data(project_dir); source(file.path(project_dir, "src", "R", "explorer_replays.R")); build_explorer_replays(project_dir); source(file.path(project_dir, "src", "R", "explorer_crossings.R")); build_explorer_crossings(project_dir); TRUE },
                      error = function(e) { fw_log("warning", "Explorer map data", conditionMessage(e), "explorer"); FALSE })
  if (grid_ok) {
    py_bin <- reticulate::py_config()$python
    nsi_script <- file.path(project_dir, "src", "python", "build_nsi_grid.py")
    if (!file.exists(file.path(project_dir, "data", "derived", "explorer", "nsi_grid.csv")) && file.exists(nsi_script))
      system2(py_bin, c(shQuote(nsi_script), "--project-dir", shQuote(project_dir)), stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE)   # one-time, about 15 min; needs internet
    status <- system2(py_bin, c(shQuote(explorer_script), "--project-dir", shQuote(project_dir),
                                "--docs-copy", shQuote(file.path(project_dir, "docs", "explorer.html"))),
                      stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE)
    if (!identical(status, 0L)) fw_log("warning", "Explorer export", "export_explorer.py failed; the previous explorer file is embedded.", "explorer")
  }
}
if (isTRUE(p$embed_explorer) && !is.na(paths$explorer) && file.exists(paths$explorer)) {
  callout("note", "About the explorer",
          "It runs entirely in your browser, with no data sent anywhere. It uses the same model as this report, so its numbers match the tables above. It explains patterns in past NOAA records; it is **not a flood forecast or warning**.")
  uri <- base64enc::dataURI(file = paths$explorer, mime = "text/html")
  cat(sprintf('<iframe src="%s" title="Carolina HighGround risk explorer" style="width:100%%; height:900px; border:1px solid #d7e0e6; border-radius:10px;" loading="lazy"></iframe>\n\n', uri))
  cat(download_link(paths$explorer, "Download the explorer (HTML) to open full-screen"))
} else {
  callout("note", "Explorer not embedded", sprintf("Expected at `%s`.", p$explorer_path))
}
```

## Modeling limitations

```{r}
#| label: limitations-flags
#| include: false
rain_used <- rung_ok("+ Rainfall")
svi_used <- rung_ok("+ Tract SVI")
imperv_year_matched <- "impervious_vintage" %in% names(model_table)
```

* **Small number of severe events.** About `r py$summary$devel_pos` high-consequence flood events in the development years; results vary noticeably across folds, and the holdout test is small.
* **`r p$highlight_event_name` dominates the test years.** `r fmt_pct(hs$share_test_positives_in_window[1])` of the test positives fall in one week, so holdout scores largely measure how well the model recognizes that single storm (see the sensitivity table above).
* **`r if (svi_used) "Mixed-scale vulnerability." else "County-level vulnerability."`** `r if (svi_used) "SOVI and population density are the same for every event in a county; the CDC/ATSDR SVI percentiles are tract-level." else "SOVI and population density are the same for every event in a county."`
* **Static layers.** `r if (imperv_year_matched) "The infrastructure and stream snapshots are static and post-date most events. Imperviousness is matched to the event year through 2023 (events from 2024 on use 2023)." else "Imperviousness (2023) and the infrastructure and stream snapshots post-date most events."`
* **`r if (rain_used) "Rainfall is coarse and describes the storm itself." else "No rainfall."`** `r if (rain_used) "gridMET daily totals on a 4 km grid smooth out short, intense bursts. Because rainfall describes the storm itself, the models explain how severe impacts are given a flood-related event; they do not forecast floods." else "The models describe where impacts are severe *given* a flood-related event, not whether a storm will flood; they are not a forecast."`
